original_question: Does every subgroup H of an infinite-dimensional Lie group G admit a smooth manifold structure making H an initial Lie subgroup of G? Here this means that, for every k in N union {infinity}, H is C^k-initial in G in the sense that the inclusion map lambda: H -> G is C^k and every map f: X -> H from a C^k-manifold X is C^k whenever lambda o f is C^k, and moreover the induced tangent map L(lambda): L(H) -> L(G) is injective.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1: whether every subgroup of an infinite-dimensional Lie group carries a Lie group structure making it an initial Lie subgroup of the ambient group; this is the exact general question your draft is aiming at, while Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 give the nearby direct-limit context and partial positive result discussed immediately afterward.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main target as the general subgroup question from the paper, keeps the quantifier over arbitrary subgroups H ≤ G, and captures the paper's initiality condition through the inclusion map λ:H→G, the C^k test via maps f:X→H, and injectivity of the induced tangent/Lie algebra map L(λ).
missing_details: The paper is working in the category of Lie groups modeled on locally convex real vector spaces; this modeling category is part of the setup.
H must be given a Lie group structure, not merely a smooth manifold structure.
The inclusion λ:H→G is the subgroup inclusion and should be understood as a smooth group homomorphism for the sought structure on H.
The question is about arbitrary subgroups H of an infinite-dimensional Lie group G, with no extra assumptions such as closedness, splitting, finite codimension, or direct-limit hypotheses.
To be fully stand-alone, L(λ) should be identified as the induced Lie algebra map at the identity.

If one wants maximal paper-faithfulness, one should note that this is posed as the infinite-dimensional analogue of the finite-dimensional initial subgroup theorem, and that Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3 discuss the special case where G is a direct limit of finite-dimensional Lie groups.
refined_question: Let G be an infinite-dimensional Lie group modeled on a locally convex real vector space, and let H ≤ G be an arbitrary subgroup. Must there exist a Lie group structure on H, modeled on a locally convex space, such that the inclusion homomorphism λ:H→G is smooth, the induced Lie algebra map L(λ):L(H)→L(G) is injective, and, for every k in N∪{infinity} and every C^k-manifold X, a map f:X→H is C^k if and only if λ∘f:X→G is C^k; i.e. does every subgroup of an infinite-dimensional Lie group admit the structure of an initial Lie subgroup of the ambient group?
justification: The draft is already very close to Conjecture 1.1, but it slightly under-specifies the paper's ambient category and says only 'smooth manifold structure' instead of a Lie group structure on H. The nearby introductory discussion is important because Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 isolate the direct-limit setting in which the conjectured phenomenon is analyzed positively, whereas the paper as a whole shows that the unrestricted conjecture fails in general. So the sharpest stand-alone reformulation is still the Conjecture 1.1 question itself, with the locally convex/Lie-group setup made explicit.
